_comment: FEAT-348 (DEF-003, US-006) accepted-known-failures manifest. Lists the EXACT set of pre-existing, out-of-scope failing-test identifiers ci/gate_exit_policy.gd's GutHookScript.run() compares against the live GUT run's failing-test set. Identifier shape: '<script res:// path>::<test method name>' (see GateExitPolicy.build_test_id). The gate exits 0 only when the actual failing set exactly equals this list -- no new/regressed entries, and no manifest entry that has unexpectedly started passing. FEAT-349 (DEF-004/DEF-006, US-007) triage note: this manifest was formally re-audited against a real `godot --headless --path <repo_root> -- --gut-run-all` run (captured 2026-07-27) specifically for the three files DEF-004/DEF-006 named as needing formal ticketing -- tests/unit/test_opportunistic_strike_initiative_ordering.gd (the 'LateSpawnHighRoll' gap, all 4 previously-failing functions), tests/integration/test_opportunistic_strike_ranged_reactor_excluded.gd, and tests/integration/test_steel_thread_scenario_boot_e2e.gd. That real run found ZERO failing tests across all three files on this HEAD -- the gaps DEF-004/DEF-006 flagged were already closed by prior iterations (see commit e42ff80 'fix(tests): migrate 4 pre-existing post-Iter-T/Q test failures to 0 failing' and FEAT-346's ExplorationModeController migration sweep, both of which landed before this triage). Per ci/gate_exit_policy.gd's own contract, adding manifest entries for tests that are ACTUALLY PASSING would itself trip the 'unexpectedly_passing' mismatch branch and turn the gate red -- so, to match the real GUT output exactly (this feature's own test_criteria), this manifest correctly remains empty. tests/integration/test_out_of_scope_regression_guard.py now pins all three files' content via a byte-identical SHA-256 baseline (tests/integration/fixtures/baseline_out_of_scope_hashes.json) so this empty-manifest state cannot silently drift without an explicit, reviewed fixture update. Remains empty: the suite has no accepted pre-existing failures as of this iteration.
